title.en: Mary Ann Shadd Cary · A press across the border
title.zh: 玛丽·安·沙德·卡里 · 跨越边境的报刊事业

location.label: Chatham, Ontario; representative Canadian publishing and community context

summary.en:
Mary Ann Shadd Cary built a public life around schools, newspapers and the rights of people crossing borders to escape slavery. Born to free Black parents in Delaware in 1823, she grew up in an abolitionist family that assisted freedom seekers. The Fugitive Slave Act of 1850 increased the danger facing both refugees and those helping them, even in American free states. Shadd arrived in Upper Canada in 1851 and taught refugee children while advocating settlement and economic independence.

In 1853 she established the Provincial Freeman, using print to challenge slavery, racial discrimination and restrictions on women. Her teaching also included a school for Black and white children. Journalism made refugee communities participants in political argument rather than simply recipients of assistance. Her Canadian work belongs alongside the longer history of Black community building on both sides of the border.

After her husband Thomas Cary died, she returned to the United States and recruited Black soldiers for the Union during the Civil War. In Washington she combined teaching, writing and legal studies at Howard University. She also organized for women’s voting rights, addressing the National Woman Suffrage Association convention in 1878. Her criticism of political arrangements that excluded women connected emancipation to continuing questions about citizenship. She died in Washington in 1893. Her life links migration, education and political participation across two countries; no single city contains the whole story.
summary.zh:
玛丽·安·沙德·卡里把学校、报纸与逃离奴役者的权利联系起来。她于1823年出生于特拉华州的自由黑人家庭，父母参与废奴活动并帮助寻求自由的人。1850年《逃奴法》使逃亡者与援助者在美国自由州也面临更大危险。沙德于1851年来到上加拿大，一面教导难民子女，一面主张通过定居和经济自主建立更稳固的生活。

1853年，她创办《省自由人报》，借助报刊反对奴隶制、种族歧视及对女性的限制。她还办过黑人与白人儿童共同就读的学校。报刊让难民社区成为政治讨论的参与者，而不仅是等待救济的群体。这段事业属于美加边境两侧黑人建立社区的长期历史。

丈夫托马斯·卡里去世后，她返回美国，在内战期间为联邦军招募黑人士兵。移居华盛顿后，她将教学、写作与霍华德大学的法律学习结合起来，并参与妇女选举权组织，1878年在全国妇女选举权协会大会发言。她批评将妇女排除在外的政治安排，使废奴后的自由进一步连接到公民资格问题。她于1893年在华盛顿去世。她的一生跨越两国，把迁移、教育和政治参与连接起来，无法由单一城市概括。

title.zh: 莎拉·温尼马卡 · 以证词反对土地剥夺

location.label: Northern Paiute country in Nevada; representative homeland context

summary.en:
Sarah Winnemucca, known to her family as Thocmetony, grew up as settler migration and mining transformed Northern Paiute homelands. Born about 1844 in present-day Nevada, she became an interpreter, teacher and public advocate. These roles placed her between communities facing very unequal power. Her work for the U.S. Army did not mean acceptance of the violence, broken promises and corrupt administration that she described.

After the 1878 conflict and the forced removal of Paiutes from the Malheur Reservation to Yakama, she sought the return of displaced people and the reunion of families. At Vancouver Barracks she also advocated for Shoshone and Bannock prisoners. Her March 1881 letter asked that they be allowed to remain with land, work and housing under military protection. This was a particular strategy for survival, distinct from the demand to restore displaced Paiutes to Malheur.

Her book Life Among the Piutes: Their Wrongs and Claims appeared in 1883. It combined personal experience, political argument and a petition that readers could circulate. Mary Mann helped edit the book, reminding readers that the published testimony also passed through a particular reform network. A petition received by Congress in January 1884 demanded restoration to Malheur and described the enduring pain of separated families.

Winnemucca died in 1891. Her career shows how an Indigenous woman used translation, performance and print to contest removal. Her account is a historically situated voice with its own strategies and judgments, not a substitute for every Paiute community’s experience.
summary.zh:
莎拉·温尼马卡在家人之间被称为托克梅托尼。她成长之际，移民和矿业正在改变北派尤特人的家园。她约于1844年出生于今内华达州，后来成为翻译、教师和公共倡议者。这些身份使她处在权力极不对等的群体之间。她为美国军队工作，并不意味着认同她所揭露的暴力、失信与行政腐败。

1878年冲突后，派尤特人被从马尔赫尔保留地强迁到雅卡马。她为流离失所者返回家园和家庭团聚奔走，她还在温哥华军营为被拘留的肖肖尼人与班诺克人争取权利。1881年3月的信要求允许这些人留在那里，在军方保护下获得土地、工作与住房。这是特定的生存策略，应同要求被迁离的派尤特人返回马尔赫尔相区别。

1883年，她出版《派尤特人的生活：他们所受的不公与诉求》，把个人经历、政治论证和读者可以传递的请愿书结合起来。玛丽·曼协助编辑，说明这份公开证词也经过特定改革网络的传播。国会于1884年1月收到的请愿书要求恢复马尔赫尔家园，描述家庭长期分离的痛苦。

温尼马卡于1891年去世。她以翻译、演讲和出版反对强迁，展现原住民女性运用多种渠道争取权利的实践。她的叙述有特定历史位置、策略与判断，不能代替每个派尤特社区的全部经验。

title.en: Dolores Huerta · Organizing workers and households
title.zh: 多洛雷斯·韦尔塔 · 组织劳动者与家庭

location.label: Delano, California; representative farmworker organizing center

summary.en:
Dolores Huerta’s early organizing connected conditions in agricultural work with the lives of children and families. Born in Dawson, New Mexico, in 1930 and raised mainly in Stockton, California, she trained as a teacher. The hunger and insecurity she encountered among farmworkers’ children helped lead her from the classroom into collective action. In 1955 she became involved in the Community Service Organization, linking local political participation to the needs of working communities.

Huerta co-founded the National Farm Workers Association with César Chávez in 1962. When Filipino workers organized through the Agricultural Workers Organizing Committee began the Delano grape strike in September 1965, the association joined them. The alliance depended on organizing across ethnic and organizational lines; neither a single leader nor a single community explains its achievements. Huerta helped build the boycott beyond the vineyards and negotiated with growers, making consumers and distant supporters part of the struggle.

The 1966 union merger and contracts won in 1970 translated mobilization into more durable institutions. Pay and working conditions were connected to protections, access to care and the practical demands of family life. Huerta also faced gender discrimination while asserting women’s role within the movement. Her work invites attention to the organizing, negotiation and unpaid care behind public demonstrations. This entry follows her formation and the grape-strike years through 1970; that endpoint is a historical focus, not the end of her life or activism.
summary.zh:
多洛雷斯·韦尔塔早期的组织工作，把农业劳动条件与儿童、家庭的生活联系起来。她于1930年出生于新墨西哥州道森，主要在加利福尼亚州斯托克顿长大，接受教师训练。农场工人子女的饥饿与生活不稳定，使她从课堂走向集体行动。1955年，她加入社区服务组织的工作，将地方政治参与同劳动社区的需要结合起来。

1962年，她与塞萨尔·查韦斯共同创立全国农场工人协会。1965年9月，农业工人组织委员会中的菲律宾裔工人在德拉诺发起葡萄采收罢工，该协会随后加入。联盟依靠跨族群、跨组织的合作，无法用单一领袖或单一社区解释。韦尔塔推动抵制运动走出葡萄园，并与种植业者谈判，让消费者与远方支持者参与斗争。

1966年的组织合并及1970年赢得的合约，使动员转化为较持久的制度。工资与劳动条件，同保障措施、医疗服务和家庭生活的实际需要相连。韦尔塔还面对性别歧视，同时坚持女性在运动中的地位。她的经历让人看到公共示威背后的组织、谈判与无偿照护劳动。本条关注她的成长及截至1970年的葡萄罢工阶段；结束年份不是她生命或行动的终点。

title.en: Hohokam canal communities · Farming an arid valley
title.zh: 霍霍坎灌渠社区 · 干旱河谷中的农耕

location.label: Salt River valley near Tempe; representative canal landscape

summary.en:
Communities that archaeologists group under the name Hohokam developed extensive farming landscapes in southern Arizona. Canals, reservoirs and other ways of managing water supported maize, beans, squash and cotton while people also gathered wild foods. Maintaining these systems required repeated work and coordination, connecting household food production to decisions beyond an individual field.

Settlements ranged from farmsteads to larger villages with shared plazas. During the earlier period, ballcourts formed part of community ceremonial life. Around the transition to the Classic period, roughly 1150, settlement layouts and building practices changed; surface adobe buildings and enclosed compounds became more prominent. Such differences show that the region did not follow one unchanging village pattern over a thousand years.

Canals and monumental features are evidence of organization, but they do not by themselves identify a single ruler or a unified empire. Archaeologists continue to debate how political authority operated between communities. The conventional 450–1450 interval describes an archaeological sequence and its changing material record. It does not date the beginning of Indigenous occupation, mark the disappearance of descendants, or turn a canal network into a territorial border.
summary.zh:
考古学家以“霍霍坎”统称的社区，在亚利桑那州南部形成了广阔的农业景观。灌渠、蓄水设施及其他管理水资源的方式，支持玉米、豆类、南瓜和棉花种植，人们也继续采集野生食物。维护这些系统需要持续劳动与协调，使家庭的食物生产同单块田地之外的共同决策连接起来。

聚落从小型农庄到具有公共广场的大村落不等。较早阶段的球场属于社区礼仪生活的一部分。约1150年进入经典期前后，聚落布局和建筑方式发生变化，地面土坯建筑及围合院落更加突出。这些差异说明，该地区并非千年不变地维持同一种村落模式。

灌渠与大型建筑证明了组织能力，却不能单凭它们确定某位统治者或统一帝国。不同社区之间的政治权威如何运作，仍是考古讨论的问题。约450—1450年的传统分期描述考古序列及其变化的物质记录，不是原住民最早居住的时间，不代表后代消失，也不能将灌渠网络直接画成领土边界。

title.en: Mimbres painted bowls · Images, makers and mortuary practice
title.zh: 明布雷斯彩绘陶碗 · 图像、制作者与丧葬实践

location.label: Mimbres Valley, New Mexico; representative production region

summary.en:
Mimbres black-on-white bowls make painting a major source for understanding communities in what is now southwestern New Mexico. Museum examples combine carefully controlled geometric designs with people, fish, birds and other living beings. Painters worked on the inside of rounded bowls, fitting images to a curved surface rather than treating decoration as a separate flat picture.

A small bowl in the Metropolitan Museum carries a spider-web design and is dated about 950–1150. A Princeton example, dated 1000–1130, depicts two people beneath or within a large fish. The museums’ interpretations show both the richness and the limits of visual evidence. Comparisons with later Pueblo narratives or Mesoamerican stories can suggest questions, but a resemblance does not establish the exact story intended by the painter or prove direct contact between distant communities.

Some bowls entered burials and were deliberately pierced. This connects ceramics to practices surrounding death as well as the skills of living makers. The dates here bracket the selected painted tradition, not all Mimbres settlement history. The valley point is regional; the records do not justify assigning these collected objects to a precise excavated household.
summary.zh:
明布雷斯黑白彩绘陶碗，使绘画成为理解今新墨西哥州西南部社区的重要材料。博物馆藏品把精细几何构图与人物、鱼、鸟及其他生命形象结合起来。绘画位于圆碗内部，需要适应弯曲表面，并非把平面图像简单附在器物上。

纽约大都会艺术博物馆的一件小碗绘有蛛网图案，年代约为950—1150年。普林斯顿的一件陶碗定为1000—1130年，描绘两个人物与一条大鱼的组合。这些馆藏研究同时显示图像证据的丰富性与局限。与较晚的普韦布洛叙事或中部美洲故事比较，可以提出问题；图像相似并不能确定制作者想表达的具体故事，也不能证明遥远社区之间曾直接接触。

部分陶碗进入墓葬，并被有意穿孔，使陶器同围绕死亡的实践及生者的制作技能相连。本条年代围绕所选彩绘传统，并非整个明布雷斯聚落史。点位代表河谷地区；馆藏记录不足以把这些器物定位到某个精确发掘的家庭。

title.en: The Cherokee Phoenix · A nation speaks in print
title.zh: 《切罗基凤凰报》 · 一个民族的印刷声音

location.label: New Echota, Georgia; historical newspaper publication center

summary.en:
The Cherokee Nation began publishing the Cherokee Phoenix at New Echota in February 1828. Its pages placed Cherokee syllabary and English text within the same newspaper, bringing written Cherokee into a recurring public forum. This was an institution of a living nation debating education, government and its future while the United States and Georgia pressed for removal.

The paper covered national government, community and religious activities, relations with other Indigenous peoples, and arguments over land. Congressional debates and court decisions appeared beside subjects closer to everyday life. Reading these materials shows that resistance was also sustained through information, editorial judgment and communication among readers.

The original newspaper ceased publication in 1834, before the forced removal of 1838. Its surviving run therefore cannot provide eyewitness reporting of that later event. Western Carolina University’s digital project transcribes selected English-language articles concerning Cherokee and regional history; it does not reproduce the whole bilingual paper. The distinction matters: a searchable modern archive offers an entry into this political world while preserving only part of what its historical readers encountered.
summary.zh:
切罗基民族于1828年2月在新埃科塔出版《切罗基凤凰报》。报纸把切罗基音节文字与英语放在同一公共版面，使书面切罗基语进入持续性的讨论空间。当美国政府与佐治亚州推动强迁时，这一仍然存续的民族正通过报刊讨论教育、治理与自身前途。

报纸报道民族政府、社区及宗教活动，与其他原住民族的关系，以及有关土地的争论。国会辩论和法院判决，同更贴近日常生活的题材并列。这些材料显示，抵抗也通过信息、编辑判断及读者之间的沟通持续展开。

原报于1834年停刊，早于1838年的强制迁移，因此不能将存世报刊当成对后来事件的现场报道。西卡罗来纳大学的数字项目转录了涉及切罗基及地区历史的部分英语文章，并未重现完整双语报纸。这个区别很重要：可检索的现代档案让人进入当时的政治世界，却只保留了历史读者所见内容的一部分。

dateNote.en: 1828–1834 is the original New Echota publication run. This interval neither dates Cherokee sovereignty nor the complete history of subsequent Cherokee newspapers.
dateNote.zh: 1828—1834年为新埃科塔原报刊行期，不代表切罗基主权的起讫，也不是后续切罗基报刊的全部历史。

title.en: Komagata Maru · Challenging an exclusionary border
title.zh: 驹形丸号 · 挑战排斥性的边境

location.label: Burrard Inlet, Vancouver; representative anchorage

summary.en:
When the Komagata Maru reached Vancouver in May 1914, its passengers confronted an immigration system designed to exclude most migrants from South Asia. The ship, chartered by Gurdit Singh, carried 376 prospective immigrants via East Asia. Canadian rules demanded a continuous journey from the country of origin and imposed a cash requirement on Asian arrivals, restrictions that worked against travel from India within the British Empire.

The passengers did not simply accept the decision. Vancouver’s South Asian community formed a shore committee, raised money and pursued a court challenge. Meanwhile those aboard endured deteriorating access to food and water. Legal argument and practical solidarity therefore developed alongside a prolonged struggle over the ship’s presence in the harbour.

After the legal challenge failed, authorities used the warship Rainbow to help force departure. The Komagata Maru left on 23 July after supplies were arranged, with most passengers denied entry. This episode connects formal imperial subjecthood to sharply unequal rights of movement. Its Vancouver point marks the confrontation at the border, not the full voyage or the separate violence that followed the ship’s return to India.
summary.zh:
1914年5月，“驹形丸号”抵达温哥华，乘客面对的是一套旨在排斥多数南亚移民的制度。古尔迪特·辛格租用该船，经东亚搭载376名希望移民的人抵达加拿大。加拿大要求从原籍国连续航行而来，并对亚洲入境者规定携带现金的门槛，使英帝国内部从印度出发的迁移受到阻碍。

乘客并未被动接受决定。温哥华南亚社区成立岸上委员会，筹措资金，并寻求法院救济。与此同时，船上的食物和饮水供应日益恶化。法律争论、实际互助与船只在港内的长期对峙同时展开。

诉讼失败后，当局借助“彩虹号”军舰迫使船只离开。补给安排完成后，“驹形丸号”于7月23日启航，多数乘客被拒绝入境。这一事件揭示帝国臣民身份与实际迁徙权利之间的巨大不平等。温哥华点位标示边境对峙，不涵盖完整航程，也不把返抵印度后的另一段暴力事件压缩成同一地点。

dateNote.en: The Vancouver confrontation ran from 23 May to 23 July 1914. The single-year interval does not summarize every stage of the voyage.
dateNote.zh: 温哥华对峙发生于1914年5月23日至7月23日。单年区间不概括整段航程的所有阶段。

sources.title: The Komagata Maru Incident of 1914
sources.evidenceNote: Inspected historical background: arrival/departure dates, 376 passengers, 1908 immigration barriers, Gurdit Singh, shore committee, failed test case, provisioning and Rainbow intervention.

en: The ship arrived with 376 prospective immigrants.
A South Asian shore committee supported the passengers.
Most were denied entry before the July departure.
zh: 船上有376名希望移民的乘客。
南亚社区岸上委员会支持乘客。
多数人在7月离港前被拒绝入境。

reviewLimit.zh: 已读加拿大公园局资料支持温哥华事件。乘客个人证词及返抵印度后的经历仍需研究；本条并非完整迁移史。

title.en: Japanese Canadians · Removal, dispossession and restricted return
title.zh: 日裔加拿大人 · 强迁、财产剥夺与返乡限制

location.label: Vancouver; representative coastal community, not a confinement camp

summary.en:
In 1942 the Canadian government removed almost 22,000 people of Japanese ancestry from the Pacific coast, including many Canadian-born citizens. Families lost homes, work and the ability to decide where they would live. Their destinations differed: interior camps, road camps and farms were parts of a dispersed system, not one common experience of imprisonment.

The government also sold property placed under its control. Dispossession made returning more difficult because houses, boats and businesses could not simply be reclaimed when the war ended. Community histories therefore connect confinement to the transfer of assets and the destruction of established livelihoods.

Restrictions continued after 1945. Japanese Canadians were pressed to move east of the Rockies or go to Japan, including people for whom Japan was not home. Freedom to return to the coast was restored in 1949, but a legal change could not rebuild every lost neighbourhood. Decades of community campaigning culminated in a federal redress agreement in 1988. The entry’s endpoint marks the lifting of movement restrictions, while the later agreement belongs to the continuing history of organizing, remembrance and accountability.
summary.zh:
1942年，加拿大政府将近2.2万名日裔居民迁离太平洋沿岸，其中许多人出生于加拿大。家庭失去住宅、工作及自主决定居住地点的权利。迁移目的地各不相同：内陆营地、筑路营和农场组成分散的制度，不能把所有经历概括为同一种拘禁。

政府还出售了交由其控制的财产。住房、渔船与企业无法在战争结束时直接取回，使返乡更加困难。因此，社区史把拘禁同资产转移及既有生计的破坏相联系。

限制在1945年以后继续。日裔加拿大人被迫在迁往落基山脉以东或前往日本之间选择，后者对许多人并非真正的家园。1949年恢复返回沿岸的自由，但法律变化无法重建所有失去的社区。经过数十年组织行动，联邦政府于1988年达成赔偿与平反协议。本条结束年份标示迁徙限制解除，而后来的协议属于仍在延续的组织、记忆与追责历史。

dateNote.en: 1942–1949 covers forced removal through restoration of movement rights. The Vancouver point represents the coastal communities affected; it is not the location of every camp.
dateNote.zh: 1942—1949年涵盖强迁至恢复迁徙权利。温哥华点位代表受影响沿岸社区，不是所有营地的位置。

Property sales deepened the damage to families and livelihoods.
Coastal return restrictions lasted until 1949.
zh: 1942年的强迁波及近2.2万人。
财产出售加重了对家庭与生计的破坏。

title.en: Delano grape strike · Filipino and Mexican American solidarity
title.zh: 德拉诺葡萄罢工 · 菲律宾裔与墨西哥裔的团结

location.label: Forty Acres near Delano; representative organizing and service center

summary.en:
Filipino farmworkers belonging to the Agricultural Workers Organizing Committee began the Delano grape strike on 8 September 1965. Organizers including Larry Itliong and Philip Vera Cruz challenged low pay and growers’ control over working conditions. Eight days later, the National Farm Workers Association joined, bringing the work of César Chávez, Dolores Huerta and many Mexican American families into a shared campaign.

A strike in the fields became a wider consumer boycott. Organizers asked supporters elsewhere to connect the food they bought with the conditions under which it was harvested. The two organizations merged into the United Farm Workers Organizing Committee in 1966, and contracts with grape growers followed in 1970.

The movement also built places where support could continue beyond a demonstration. Forty Acres housed organizing and service activities, including access to medical care and hiring arrangements; later retirement housing responded to the circumstances of older Filipino workers. These institutions reveal the household and community dimensions of labour politics. The settlement was a major achievement, but 1970 did not end agricultural inequality or the continuing work required to maintain collective representation.
summary.zh:
1965年9月8日，农业工人组织委员会中的菲律宾裔农场工人在德拉诺发动葡萄采收罢工。拉里·伊特利翁、菲利普·维拉克鲁斯等组织者挑战低工资及种植业者对劳动条件的控制。八天后，全国农场工人协会加入，塞萨尔·查韦斯、多洛雷斯·韦尔塔及许多墨西哥裔家庭的行动汇入共同斗争。

田间罢工发展为更广泛的消费者抵制。组织者请外地支持者把购买的食物与收获这些食物的劳动条件联系起来。两个组织于1966年合并为联合农场工人组织委员会，并于1970年与葡萄种植业者达成合约。

运动还建立了能够在示威之后继续提供支持的场所。“四十英亩”基地承载组织及服务活动，包括医疗与雇工安排；后来的退休住宅回应了年长菲律宾裔工人的处境。这些设施揭示劳动政治的家庭与社区层面。和解是一项重要成果，但1970年并未终结农业劳动中的不平等，也没有消除维持集体代表机制所需的持续工作。

dateNote.en: 1965–1970 spans the grape strike and principal contract settlement. Forty Acres represents a movement center; the boycott and agricultural workforce extended far beyond it.
dateNote.zh: 1965—1970年涵盖葡萄罢工及主要合约达成阶段。四十英亩代表运动中心；抵制范围与农业劳动者分布远超此地。

title.en: Gulf of Georgia Cannery · A multilingual working waterfront
title.zh: 乔治亚湾罐头厂 · 多族群劳动的滨水社区

location.label: Gulf of Georgia Cannery, Steveston; industrial site

summary.en:
The Gulf of Georgia Cannery opened at Steveston in 1894, joining a fishing industry built on the lands and waters of the Musqueam people. Its history links the movement of fish and preserved food to the work of people whose contributions differed by community, gender and occupation. A cannery depended on much more than the machinery visible inside its walls.

Indigenous fishers and workers, Chinese processing workers, Japanese Canadian fishing and boatbuilding families, and women from several communities helped sustain the waterfront. Boats, seasonal work, processing lines and household labour connected the factory to a wider settlement. Canned salmon entered distant markets, while local livelihoods depended on changing fisheries and industrial demand.

The site’s working life continued until 1979 and included herring reduction as well as salmon canning. These changes caution against imagining the building performing one identical task for its entire existence. Interpreting the cannery alongside immigration exclusion and the wartime removal of Japanese Canadians also changes what an industrial landmark can show: technology was embedded in a social world whose participants did not enjoy equal security or rights.
summary.zh:
乔治亚湾罐头厂于1894年在史蒂夫斯顿开业，进入一个建立在穆斯奎姆人土地与水域上的渔业体系。其历史把鱼类和加工食品的流通，同按社区、性别及职业呈现不同分工的劳动联系起来。罐头厂依靠的远不只是厂房内可见的机械。

原住民渔民与工人、华裔加工工人、日裔加拿大渔业和造船家庭，以及多个社区的女性，共同维持滨水地区的运转。渔船、季节性雇佣、加工线和家庭劳动，把工厂与更广阔的聚落相连。罐装鲑鱼进入远方市场，而地方生计依赖不断变化的鱼类资源及工业需求。

场址生产持续到1979年，既包括鲑鱼罐装，也包括鲱鱼加工提炼。这些变化提醒人们，不应想象建筑在全部使用期间都执行相同任务。将罐头厂同移民排斥及战时日裔加拿大人的强迁并读，工业地标就能呈现更多内容：技术嵌入一个社会世界，参与其中的人并不享有同等安全与权利。

dateNote.en: 1894–1979 is the site’s industrial operating interval, including changes in production. The point is the cannery, not the whole fishing or labour network.
dateNote.zh: 1894—1979年为场址工业运行期，期间生产方式有变。点位为罐头厂，不代表全部渔业与劳动网络。

Several communities contributed distinct forms of work.

title.en: José Martí · Poetry, exile and Cuban independence
title.zh: 何塞·马蒂 · 诗歌、流亡与古巴独立

location.label: Havana; birth and early political-writing context

summary.en:
José Martí’s life joined literary work to organizing for Cuban independence from Spain. Born in Havana in 1853, he entered political writing while still young. In 1869 he published La Patria Libre, and imprisonment and forced labour followed his involvement in the independence cause. Exile in Spain gave him further education and another setting in which to criticize colonial punishment.

From 1881, New York became a long-term base for his writing and political activity. He reported and commented for Latin American readers while developing poetry and essays. This was not simply an interruption before a return to Cuba: the work of an exile depended on newspapers, readers and organizations distributed across borders. His career makes the city part of Caribbean and Latin American intellectual history as well as U.S. history.

In 1892 he helped establish the Cuban Revolutionary Party to organize renewed resistance. Writing and organizational work now served an effort to connect dispersed supporters with the struggle on the island. War resumed in 1895, and Martí returned to Cuba. He died in fighting at Dos Ríos in May, before the outcome of the conflict.

His death did not make his different roles interchangeable. Poems, journalistic observations and political appeals addressed different audiences and deserve to be read in their own contexts. Following those connections reveals the work required to turn a movement’s aspirations into a shared public language, while avoiding the assumption that every later political use of Martí’s image expressed his own intentions.
summary.zh:
何塞·马蒂把文学创作与争取古巴脱离西班牙的组织工作结合起来。他于1853年出生于哈瓦那，年轻时便开始政治写作。1869年，他出版《自由祖国》；随后因参与独立事业而遭监禁和苦役。流亡西班牙期间，他继续求学，也获得了批评殖民惩罚制度的另一处阵地。

自1881年起，纽约成为其长期写作与政治活动基地。他为拉丁美洲读者报道和评论，同时创作诗歌与散文。这并非等待返回古巴期间的一段空白：流亡者的事业依靠跨境分布的报纸、读者与组织。通过他，纽约也成为加勒比与拉丁美洲思想史的一部分。

1892年，他协助建立古巴革命党，为重新抵抗殖民统治组织力量。写作与组织活动将分散的支持者同岛上的斗争连接起来。战争于1895年重启，他返回古巴，同年5月在多斯里奥斯战斗中去世，未能看到冲突的结局。

他的死亡并未使各种身份变得可以互换。诗歌、新闻观察与政治呼吁面对不同读者，应放在各自情境中阅读。追踪这些联系，可以看见把运动理想转化为共同公共语言所需的工作，也避免把后来对马蒂形象的每一种政治使用都当成他本人的意愿。

dateNote.en: 1853–1895 is the reported lifespan. New York milestones mark an established writing and organizing base; Dos Ríos is an approximate locality rather than a reconstructed battlefield position.

title.en: Carolina Maria de Jesus · Writing the city from its margins
title.zh: 卡罗利娜·玛丽亚·德热苏斯 · 从城市边缘书写生活

location.label: Canindé, São Paulo; representative writing and household context

summary.en:
Carolina Maria de Jesus made the everyday struggle for food, housing and dignity a subject of Brazilian literature. Born in Sacramento, Minas Gerais, in 1914, she later lived in São Paulo. In the Canindé favela she raised three children and earned money collecting paper and other recoverable materials. Writing developed within that demanding routine rather than after she had escaped it.

She was already seeking a public literary voice before the book that made her famous: a poem appeared in a newspaper in 1940. Quarto de despejo, published in 1960, brought her diaries to a wide readership. The following year, Casa de alvenaria continued her account from a changed social position. Moving between those books complicates an easy story in which publication permanently solves poverty or makes an author accepted by the literary establishment.

Her work extended beyond the image of a diary writer discovered by someone else. The archive includes poetry and other literary forms, compositions and reflections on the society around her. Scholars also examine the editorial choices through which manuscripts reached print. Published language should therefore not be assumed to reproduce every manuscript decision unchanged.

Carolina died in 1977 in the São Paulo area. Her writing lets readers approach urban history through the decisions of a Black woman supporting a household, observing racial and economic inequality, and insisting on intellectual authorship. Her life connects literature with the material systems of the city: discarded paper, insecure housing, work, schooling and the struggle to be heard.
summary.zh:
卡罗利娜·玛丽亚·德热苏斯把日常争取食物、住房与尊严的努力写入巴西文学。她于1914年出生于米纳斯吉拉斯州萨克拉门托，后来居住在圣保罗。在卡宁德贫民社区，她抚养三个孩子，靠收集废纸及其他可回收材料维生。写作在艰难日常之中展开，并不是脱离贫困之后才开始的活动。

在使她闻名的作品之前，她已经寻找公开的文学声音：1940年一首诗见诸报端。1960年出版的《垃圾房》使日记获得广泛读者；次年的《砖房》继续叙述社会处境改变后的生活。将两本书并读，会发现出版并不必然永久解决贫困，也不保证作者获得文学界充分接纳。

她的创作远超“被别人发现的日记作者”这一形象。档案保留诗歌、其他文学形式、音乐创作及对周遭社会的思考。学者也研究手稿转为印刷文本时的编辑选择，因此不应把出版语言理解为毫无改动的手稿复制。

她于1977年在圣保罗地区去世。通过她的写作，读者可以从一名支撑家庭、观察种族与经济不平等并坚持知识创作权的黑人女性视角理解城市史。她把文学同城市的物质体系相连：废纸、不稳定住房、劳动、教育，以及争取被倾听的努力。

title.en: Claudia Jones · Caribbean politics across three societies
title.zh: 克劳迪娅·琼斯 · 跨越三地的加勒比政治人生

location.label: Belmont, Port of Spain; birthplace anchoring a Caribbean diaspora biography

summary.en:
Claudia Jones carried Caribbean experience into movements for racial, labour and women’s rights in the United States and Britain. Born Claudia Cumberbatch in Port of Spain in 1915, she moved to New York with her family in 1924. Poverty and racism shaped her Harlem upbringing. She joined the Communist Party in 1936 and developed a career in journalism and organizing, including work for the Daily Worker.

Jones’s politics connected race, gender and class rather than treating each as an isolated question. Her writing and organizing placed Black women within arguments about work, power and collective emancipation. Anti-communist prosecution and her immigration status made her vulnerable to imprisonment and expulsion. In 1955 she was deported to Britain, where she began another phase of political and community work.

She founded the West Indian Gazette in 1958. The newspaper gave Caribbean communities a forum for confronting discrimination and imagining a shared public presence. After racist violence that year, Jones and collaborators organized an indoor Caribbean carnival at St Pancras Town Hall in January 1959. Music and celebration became part of the work of solidarity. These events helped shape later carnival traditions, but the outdoor Notting Hill carnival began after her death and had additional organizers.

Jones died in London in 1964. Her life connects the Caribbean, Harlem and London through print, organizing and forced migration. Reading her own political arguments alongside accounts produced by surveillance agencies also raises a central historical question: who gets to define an activist’s motives and legacy?
summary.zh:
克劳迪娅·琼斯把加勒比经验带入美国与英国的种族、劳动及妇女权利运动。她原名克劳迪娅·坎伯巴奇，1915年出生于西班牙港，1924年随家人迁往纽约。哈莱姆的贫困与种族主义塑造了她的成长。1936年，她加入共产党，随后从事新闻与组织工作，包括为《工人日报》写作。

她把种族、性别与阶级联系起来，而非视为互不相干的问题。她的文章与行动，使黑人女性进入关于劳动、权力和集体解放的讨论。反共起诉加上移民身份，使她面临监禁与驱逐。1955年，她被遣送到英国，开始新的政治与社区工作阶段。

1958年，她创办《西印度公报》，为加勒比社区提供反对歧视、形成共同公共声音的平台。同年发生种族主义暴力之后，她与合作者于1959年1月在圣潘克拉斯市政厅举办室内加勒比狂欢节。音乐与庆祝成为建立团结的一部分。这些活动影响了后来的狂欢节传统，但诺丁山街头狂欢节在她去世之后才出现，并有其他组织者参与。

琼斯于1964年在伦敦去世。她通过出版、组织与被迫迁移，把加勒比、哈莱姆和伦敦相连。将她本人的政治论述与监视机关制作的记录并读，也提出历史研究的重要问题：谁有权界定一位行动者的动机与遗产？

title.en: Joya de Cerén · A village preserved beyond royal history
title.zh: 霍亚德塞伦 · 王室历史之外的村落生活

location.label: Joya de Cerén, El Salvador; excavated settlement

summary.en:
A volcanic eruption buried the farming settlement now called Joya de Cerén around 600 CE. The preserved buildings and household materials provide an unusual view of everyday life in a Maya community. Instead of beginning with royal monuments, historians can ask how people stored food, cooked, worked and shared spaces.

Excavated remains include houses, storage buildings, kitchens, a sweat bath and structures used for communal purposes. Their arrangement allows comparison between the activities of households and those of a larger settlement. Earthen construction and traces of perishable materials are especially valuable because such evidence often survives less clearly than stone temples or elite tombs.

Burial by ash created a particular archaeological record; it did not freeze every aspect of social life in a form that can be read without interpretation. The relationship between buildings, objects and daily routines still requires careful analysis. Modern discovery and excavation are also separate from the ancient event. This entry centers the village’s occupied landscape before its burial, showing how the history of Mesoamerica can be approached through ordinary productive and domestic spaces as well as the affairs of rulers.
summary.zh:
约公元600年，一场火山喷发掩埋了今天称为霍亚德塞伦的农业聚落。保存下来的建筑与家用材料，为理解玛雅社区日常生活提供了少见窗口。历史研究可以从食物储存、烹饪、劳动及共享空间出发，而不仅以王室纪念建筑为起点。

出土遗存包括住宅、仓储建筑、厨房、汗浴房及具有共同用途的建筑。空间安排让人比较家庭活动与更大聚落的关系。土构建筑及易腐材料痕迹尤其珍贵，因为它们往往不像石质神庙或精英墓葬那样容易保存。

火山灰形成了特定考古记录，却没有把社会生活的每个方面都冻结成无需解释的答案。建筑、物品与日常程序之间的关系仍须细致分析。现代发现与发掘也应同古代事件区分。本条关注掩埋前有人生活的村落景观，展示中部美洲历史既可以通过统治者的活动，也可以通过普通生产与家庭空间来理解。

title.en: Garifuna communities · Displacement and musical continuity
title.zh: 加里富纳社区 · 流离与音乐传承

location.label: Dangriga, Belize; one documented recording community, not the full diaspora

summary.en:
British deportation from Saint Vincent in 1797 carried Garifuna people to islands off the Honduran coast. Communities subsequently developed along the Central American mainland, creating connections among places now in several countries. This forced movement should not be mistaken for the disappearance of a people: family life, language and cultural practice continued through new settlements and later migration.

Music provides one way to follow that continuity without treating it as unchanging. Garifuna repertoires bring together different histories of contact, movement and belief. Songs can concern travel, longing, death and relationships, while drumming and performance have particular social and ritual settings. Recording a song preserves sound but does not automatically preserve all the circumstances that give it meaning.

A Smithsonian-distributed collection draws on field recordings made in 1981 in Dangriga, Seine Bight, Hopkins and Barranco in Belize. Those recordings anchor the later end of this entry’s selected window. They offer evidence of active cultural life long after forced removal, while representing only certain performers, places and occasions. The map point selects one recording community, not a territorial capital or a boundary around Garifuna belonging.
summary.zh:
1797年，英国将加里富纳人从圣文森特驱逐到洪都拉斯外海岛屿。随后形成的中美洲沿海社区，连接了今天分属数国的地方。这种被迫迁移不能被误读为一个族群的消失：家庭、语言与文化实践在新的定居地及后来的迁移中继续发展。

音乐提供了一种追踪延续而不把文化视为静止的方法。加里富纳曲目汇集不同的接触、流动与信仰历史。歌曲可涉及旅行、思念、死亡与人际关系，鼓乐和表演也有各自的社会及仪式场景。录下声音并不自动保存赋予它意义的所有情境。

史密森学会发行的一套唱片使用1981年在伯利兹丹格里加、塞恩湾、霍普金斯与巴兰科采录的材料。这些录音构成本条所选窗口的后端，证明强迁很久之后仍然活跃的文化生活，同时仅代表特定表演者、地点与场合。地图选取其中一个录音社区，不表示领土首都，也不划定加里富纳归属的边界。

title.en: Building the Panama Canal · Labour beneath the engineering
title.zh: 修筑巴拿马运河 · 工程背后的劳动

location.label: Gatún, Panama; representative canal construction zone

summary.en:
The U.S. construction of the Panama Canal between 1904 and 1914 depended on a workforce recruited across the Caribbean, Europe and elsewhere. Canal Authority recruitment tables show the importance of the Antilles, especially Barbados. The canal’s movement of ships would rest on an earlier movement of workers and on the households that sustained them.

Employment was organized through the so-called gold and silver rolls. These categories combined differences of pay and occupation with racial and national hierarchies. Archival research shows that Black workers could be confined to the silver roll even when performing skilled work. The division also affected housing and services, extending workplace inequality into everyday life.

This history changes the question asked of an engineering landmark. Excavation volumes and locks alone do not explain who bore the burdens of construction or how the Canal Zone operated socially. Official payroll and recruitment records make some of those arrangements visible, while leaving many individual experiences harder to recover. The point at Gatún represents one major construction area; the labour system crossed a much larger zone and the sea routes that supplied it.
summary.zh:
美国于1904—1914年修筑巴拿马运河，依靠从加勒比、欧洲及其他地区招募的劳动者。运河管理机构的招工表显示，安的列斯群岛、尤其巴巴多斯具有重要地位。后来船只的通行，建立在更早的劳工迁移及支撑他们的家庭之上。

雇佣通过所谓“金名册”与“银名册”组织。这些类别把工资、职业差别同种族及国籍等级结合起来。档案研究显示，黑人劳动者即使从事技术工作，也可能被限制在银名册之内。区别还延伸到住房与服务，使职场不平等进入日常生活。

这种历史改变了理解工程地标时提出的问题。开挖量与船闸并不足以解释谁承担建设负担，以及运河区如何作为社会运作。官方工资与招工档案使部分制度可见，却也留下许多难以恢复的个人经历。加通点位代表一个重要施工区；劳动体系覆盖更大地带，并连接提供劳工的海上路线。

dateNote.en: 1904–1914 is the U.S. construction phase. Gatún is representative, not a pin for every worker, camp or recruitment port.

title.en: Cuba’s 1961 literacy campaign · Learning preserved in an archive
title.zh: 古巴1961年扫盲运动 · 档案中的学习

location.label: Havana; national organizing and later archival context

summary.en:
Cuba’s 1961 literacy campaign treated learning to read and write as a national mobilization. Its surviving documentation allows the campaign to be examined through the materials used in teaching and through the written traces left by learners. This approach connects a major political project with smaller encounters between people, texts and new skills.

The National Literacy Museum preserves manuals, primers, correspondence and other records. The teaching materials include the Cartilla Venceremos and Manual Alfabeticemos; letters addressed to Fidel Castro form another part of the collection. Such sources reveal how education was organized and how learning was presented within the revolutionary public sphere. They are also selected records shaped by the institutions that created and preserved them.

A campaign’s declared success and the experience of an individual learner are different historical questions. The archive provides routes for investigating both, but an inventory cannot by itself establish what every participant learned or believed. This entry therefore focuses on the campaign as an educational mobilization and a documented set of practices, without substituting a single literacy percentage for the diversity of lives involved.
summary.zh:
古巴1961年的扫盲运动把学习读写作为全国性动员。留存文献使人能够通过教材及学习者留下的文字来考察运动，将宏大政治工程同人、文本和新技能之间的具体相遇连接起来。

国家扫盲博物馆保存教学手册、识字课本、书信及其他记录。材料包括《我们必胜》识字课本与扫盲教学手册；写给菲德尔·卡斯特罗的信件也是馆藏的一部分。这些来源显示教育如何被组织，以及学习如何在革命公共空间中被呈现。它们同时是经创造与保存机构选择的记录。

运动宣称的成果与个别学习者的经验，是不同的历史问题。档案为两者提供研究路径，但馆藏目录本身无法说明每一位参与者学会或相信了什么。因此，本条关注作为教育动员及具体实践的扫盲运动，不以单一识字率数字代替参与者多样的生命经历。

dateNote.en: 1961 is the campaign year. Havana marks national/archival context, not a claim that teaching occurred only in the capital.
dateNote.zh: 1961年为运动年份。哈瓦那点位标示全国组织与档案背景，不表示教学只发生在首都。

title.zh: 墨西哥1968年 · 学生组织与特拉特洛尔科

location.label: Plaza de las Tres Culturas, Tlatelolco; massacre site

summary.en:
Mexico’s student movement of 1968 grew from confrontation with police into a wider demand for political freedoms. Students from institutions including the National Autonomous University and the National Polytechnic Institute organized assemblies and a National Strike Council. Their demands included the release of political prisoners, an end to repression and public dialogue.

The movement created new forms of coordination rather than relying on one charismatic figure. Demonstrations, meetings and communication between schools made participation visible in public space. Military occupation of university facilities in September sharpened the confrontation between students and the state.

On 2 October, forces attacked a gathering at the Plaza de las Tres Culturas in Tlatelolco. The massacre, shortly before the Olympic Games opened in Mexico City, became a lasting point of reference in struggles over state violence and historical memory. The number killed remains disputed; this record does not offer a false exact total. The plaza pin marks the violence, while the wider movement included many institutions, neighbourhoods and people whose experiences cannot be reduced to one day. Ending the date interval in 1968 does not end the history of demands for truth and accountability.
summary.zh:
墨西哥1968年的学生运动，从与警察的冲突发展为争取政治自由的更广泛行动。国立自治大学、国立理工学院等机构的学生组织大会与全国罢工委员会。诉求包括释放政治犯、停止镇压及开展公开对话。

运动形成新的协调方式，而非依靠单一魅力领袖。示威、集会与校际交流，使参与在公共空间中变得可见。9月军队占领大学设施，使学生与国家之间的冲突进一步加剧。

10月2日，武装力量袭击特拉特洛尔科三文化广场的集会。屠杀发生于墨西哥城奥运会开幕前不久，成为有关国家暴力与历史记忆斗争的重要参照。死亡人数仍有争议，本条不提供虚假的精确总数。广场点位标示暴力发生地，而更广泛的运动涉及许多院校、街区与个人，不能缩减为一天。1968年的区间结束，也不意味着争取真相与追责的历史结束。

dateNote.en: 1968 covers the movement and 2 October massacre. Exact casualties are unresolved; the mapped plaza is one event site within a much wider movement.
dateNote.zh: 1968年涵盖运动与10月2日屠杀。精确伤亡数字未定；广场是广泛运动中的一个事件地点。

title.en: Mexican muralism · Public walls and social arguments
title.zh: 墨西哥壁画运动 · 公共墙面与社会论辩

location.label: Mexico City; representative center of early public commissions

summary.en:
After the Mexican Revolution, public mural commissions made walls into places for arguing about the nation’s past and future. Painters used large-scale images of work, Indigenous histories, revolution and everyday life to address audiences beyond the private art market. Government sponsorship helped create these opportunities, while also making patronage and political purpose part of the works’ history.

José Clemente Orozco, Diego Rivera and David Alfaro Siqueiros developed different approaches; treating them as one voice would flatten the movement’s debates. Their travels and commissions in the United States between the late 1920s and 1940 widened its influence. Artists and publics encountered Mexican work amid the Great Depression and arguments over social inequality.

Rivera’s 1931 Agrarian Leader Zapata, made as a portable fresco, shows that mural practice could also move away from a permanently fixed wall. Its imagery constructs an interpretation of peasant struggle rather than a transparent photograph of the revolution. Following murals across buildings, exhibitions and borders makes it possible to study both artistic techniques and the political choices through which a public learns to imagine history.
summary.zh:
墨西哥革命之后，公共壁画委托把墙面变为讨论国家过去与未来的场所。画家用劳动、原住民历史、革命及日常生活的大型图像，面向私人艺术市场之外的观众。政府资助创造机会，也使赞助关系与政治目的成为作品历史的一部分。

何塞·克莱门特·奥罗斯科、迭戈·里维拉与大卫·阿尔法罗·西凯罗斯发展出不同方式，不能把他们压成同一种声音。二十世纪二十年代末至1940年前后的美国活动与委托扩大了影响。美国艺术家和公众在大萧条及社会不平等争论中接触墨西哥作品。

里维拉1931年的《农民领袖萨帕塔》采用可移动湿壁画形式，说明壁画实践也可以离开永久固定的墙面。其形象是在解释农民斗争，并非对革命的透明摄影。追踪壁画在建筑、展览与边境之间的移动，能够同时考察艺术技术，以及公众据以想象历史的政治选择。

dateNote.en: 1920–1945 is an editorial focus on early postrevolutionary public art and cross-border influence, not the beginning or end of Mexican mural painting.
dateNote.zh: 1920—1945年为革命后早期公共艺术及跨境影响的编辑关注期，不是墨西哥壁画的绝对起讫。

title.en: Taquile textiles · Teaching a living tradition
title.zh: 塔基莱纺织 · 传授活态传统

location.label: Taquile Island, Lake Titicaca; community and project setting

summary.en:
Textile making on Taquile Island links skill, memory and social life in the high Andes. Knitted hats such as the chullo and other garments carry meanings that exceed their value as goods. The transmission of knowledge depends on people learning techniques and understanding when and how particular textiles are used.

A documented project between 2006 and 2009 sought to strengthen this intergenerational transmission. Supported through the UNESCO/Japan Funds-in-Trust, it proposed a community inventory, a local research team, meetings between generations, educational materials and documentation of oral memory and social practices. These aims foreground makers as bearers of knowledge rather than treating textiles only as objects collected elsewhere.

The project description also identified pressures associated with tourism, changing materials and production for sale. Those concerns should not imply that commercial activity automatically destroys tradition or that a living community must remain unchanged. They explain why people and institutions were debating the terms of transmission. The project ended in June 2009; the date marks a particular safeguarding effort, not the end of Taquile’s textile work or the islanders’ capacity to adapt it.
summary.zh:
塔基莱岛的纺织把高安第斯地区的技能、记忆与社会生活联系起来。丘略针织帽及其他服饰的意义，超出作为商品的价值。知识传递既依靠技术学习，也依靠理解某种纺织品在何时、如何使用。

一项有记录的2006—2009年项目，旨在加强这种代际传承。项目由联合国教科文组织与日本信托基金支持，计划开展社区清单、地方研究团队、跨代会面、教材，以及口述记忆和社会实践的记录。这些目标把制作者视为知识承载者，而不仅把纺织品当作被外界收藏的物件。

项目说明也提出旅游、材料变化及面向销售生产带来的压力。这些担忧不等于商业必然摧毁传统，也不意味着活态社区必须保持不变；它们解释了人们与机构为何讨论传承条件。项目于2009年6月结束，这个日期只标示一项具体保护工作的结束，而非塔基莱纺织或岛民适应能力的终点。

dateNote.zh: 2006—2009年为有据可查的传承项目期，项目于2009年6月结束；不表示纺织传统的起源或寿命。

title.en: Eddie Koiki Mabo · Education, land and a legal challenge
title.zh: 埃迪·科伊基·马博 · 教育、土地与法律挑战

location.label: Mer, Torres Strait; homeland and land-knowledge context

summary.en:
Eddie Koiki Mabo’s challenge to Australian land law began from relationships to a particular island and community. Born on Mer in the Torres Strait in 1936, he grew up with Meriam knowledge of land, inheritance and responsibility. Those understandings differed sharply from a legal order that treated Indigenous interests as if they had not existed when British sovereignty was asserted.

In Townsville, Mabo worked in several roles and became active in community life. In 1972 authorities prevented his family from continuing from Thursday Island to Mer to visit his ill father. He helped establish the Black Community School in 1973, bringing education into the struggle for recognition and self-determination. His work at James Cook University also created encounters through which he learned how Australian law characterized the land he understood as belonging to his people.

In 1982, Mabo joined David Passi, Celuia Mapo Salee, Sam Passi and James Rice in bringing a case concerning Mer. The litigation lasted a decade and involved more than the work of a single claimant. Mabo died in January 1992, before the High Court delivered its June judgment recognizing that native title could survive the acquisition of sovereignty.

The ruling did not automatically return all Australian land or erase the effects of dispossession. Its importance lies in the legal change it enabled and the histories it required the courts to confront. Mabo’s biography is therefore larger than one courtroom result: it includes family knowledge, education, community organizing and the insistence that an imposed legal description was not the only account of a homeland.
summary.zh:
埃迪·科伊基·马博对澳大利亚土地法的挑战，源于他与特定岛屿及社区的关系。他于1936年出生于托雷斯海峡的梅尔岛，在梅里亚姆人有关土地、继承与责任的知识中成长。这些理解同英国宣布主权时把原住民土地权益视若不存在的法律秩序形成冲突。

在汤斯维尔，马博从事多种工作并参与社区生活。1972年，当局阻止全家从星期四岛继续前往梅尔，探望病中的父亲。1973年，他协助建立黑人社区学校，将教育带入争取承认与自决的实践。他在詹姆斯·库克大学工作期间的接触，也使他了解到澳大利亚法律如何描述他认为属于自己人民的土地。

1982年，马博与戴维·帕西、塞卢亚·马波·萨利、萨姆·帕西及詹姆斯·赖斯共同提起涉及梅尔岛的诉讼。案件历时十年，远非单一原告的工作。他于1992年1月去世，未能看到高等法院6月作出承认原住民地权可在主权取得后继续存在的判决。

判决并未自动返还澳大利亚全部土地，也没有抹去剥夺造成的后果。它的重要性在于促成法律变化，并要求法院正视过去的历史。马博的传记因此大于一次庭审结果：还包括家庭知识、教育、社区组织，以及坚持外来法律描述并非家园唯一解释的努力。

dateNote.en: 1936–1992 is the lifespan. The June 1992 decision occurred after his January death; it is stated as legacy, not an action he witnessed. Mer and Townsville points serve different biographical contexts.
dateNote.zh: 1936—1992年为生卒年。1992年6月判决在他1月去世之后作出，作为后续影响叙述，而非他亲历的行动。梅尔与汤斯维尔分别标示不同生平背景。

title.en: Pearl Gibbs · From domestic service to public advocacy
title.zh: 珀尔·吉布斯 · 从家政劳动走向公共倡议

location.label: Dubbo, New South Wales; representative later community-work center

summary.en:
Pearl Mary Gibbs built political experience through work, personal encounters and sustained support for other Aboriginal people. Born in 1901, she entered domestic service as a young woman. Contact with Aboriginal girls placed in service under the protection system exposed the coercion behind official claims of care. During the Depression she also worked among rural labourers, broadening the relationships on which her advocacy depended.

Gibbs joined the Aborigines Progressive Association and took part in the 1938 Day of Mourning in Sydney. She used meetings, lobbying and public communication to challenge discrimination in schooling, hospitals, employment and civic life. Her 1941 radio address offered another way to reach listeners beyond an organized meeting.

In 1954 she became the first woman to serve on the New South Wales Aborigines Welfare Board, remaining until 1957. Working within an official body was one part of her strategy, not the whole of it. In 1956 she helped form the Aboriginal-Australian Fellowship with Faith Bandler, creating a further platform for cooperation and reform. In Dubbo she helped establish a hostel in 1960 for Aboriginal people coming to town, including those needing medical treatment and their families.

She died in 1983. Her life joins the public history of protest to quieter forms of practical provision. Advocacy concerned not only formal recognition but where a person could stay, whether a child could attend school, and who controlled the conditions of a young woman’s labour.
summary.zh:
珀尔·玛丽·吉布斯通过劳动、个人接触及持续帮助其他原住民积累政治经验。她于1901年出生，年轻时从事家政劳动。接触被保护制度安排从事家务服务的原住民女孩，使她看到官方“照顾”说辞背后的强制。大萧条期间，她还在乡村劳动者之间工作，扩大了支撑倡议行动的关系网络。

吉布斯加入原住民进步协会，并参与1938年悉尼哀悼日。她借助会议、游说与公共传播，挑战学校、医院、就业及公民生活中的歧视。1941年的电台演说，使她能接触组织会议之外的听众。

1954年，她成为新南威尔士州原住民福利委员会首位女性成员，任职至1957年。进入官方机构只是策略的一部分。1956年，她与费思·班德勒共同建立原住民—澳大利亚人联谊会，提供合作与改革的另一个平台。1960年，她在达博协助建立旅舍，帮助来到城里的原住民，包括需要就医者及其家属。

她于1983年去世。她的一生把公开抗争同较少显眼的实际服务相连。倡议不仅涉及正式承认，还涉及一个人在哪里住宿、儿童能否入学，以及谁有权控制年轻女性的劳动条件。

dateNote.zh: 1901—1983年为生卒年。悉尼与达博节点区分公共抗争、官方任职及地方服务，不暗示固定不变的政治中心。

title.en: Āpirana Ngata · Land, language and political compromise
title.zh: 阿皮拉纳·恩加塔 · 土地、语言与政治折衷

location.label: East Coast, Aotearoa New Zealand; representative Ngāti Porou homeland

summary.en:
Āpirana Ngata sought ways for Māori communities to retain land and strengthen cultural life while working within New Zealand’s parliamentary system. Born at Te Araroa in 1874 and belonging to Ngāti Porou, he combined university and legal education with close engagement in East Coast community affairs. His 1893 university degree became one part of a much wider practical career.

Elected to represent Eastern Māori in 1905, he promoted land consolidation, cooperative organization and farming development. These policies tried to make landholding economically workable without simply surrendering remaining Māori land. Their consequences varied between communities, and his approach did not represent every Māori political position. His public career also depended on household work and support, including the responsibilities carried by his wife Arihia.

Cultural activity was central rather than decorative. Ngata collected and annotated waiata, encouraged carving and meeting-house projects, and supported the training of artists. The recovery and circulation of knowledge accompanied economic proposals. As Native Minister from 1928, he expanded state-supported land development. An inquiry into the administration of these schemes led to his resignation in 1934; this should not be simplified into an unsupported claim that he personally stole funds.

Ngata remained an influential figure until his death in 1950. His life shows both the possibilities and costs of institutional reform: cooperation with the state could secure resources while creating new dependencies, disagreements and demands for accountability. Land, cultural transmission and political strategy remained inseparable questions.
summary.zh:
阿皮拉纳·恩加塔试图在新西兰议会制度内，为毛利社区保有土地并加强文化生活寻找途径。他于1874年出生于特阿拉罗阿，属于恩加蒂波罗部族，将大学与法律教育同东海岸社区事务结合起来。1893年的大学学位，只是后来广泛实践事业的一部分。

1905年当选东部毛利选区议员后，他推动土地整理、合作组织与农业发展。这些政策试图在不轻易放弃剩余毛利土地的情况下，使土地经营具有经济可行性。不同社区的结果并不相同，他的方式也不能代表所有毛利政治立场。公共事业还依赖家庭劳动和支持，包括妻子阿里希亚承担的责任。

文化活动是核心而非装饰。他收集并注释毛利歌曲，鼓励雕刻及会堂建设，支持艺术人才培养。知识的恢复与传播，同经济方案一起展开。1928年出任原住民事务部长后，他扩大国家资助的土地开发。有关计划管理的调查导致他于1934年辞职；不能把它简化为没有依据的个人侵吞资金说法。

恩加塔直到1950年去世前仍具有影响力。他的一生显示制度改革的可能与代价：与国家合作能取得资源，也可能产生新的依赖、分歧及追责要求。土地、文化传承与政治策略始终是相互交织的问题。

title.en: Sālote Tupou III · Monarchy, poetry and Pacific relationships
title.zh: 萨洛特·图普三世 · 王权、诗歌与太平洋关系

location.label: Nukuʻalofa, Tongatapu; representative royal and cultural context

summary.en:
Sālote Tupou III’s life connects Tongan monarchy with poetry, performance and relationships across the Pacific. Born in 1900, she went to school in Auckland in 1909 and maintained ties with New Zealand thereafter. An Auckland newspaper’s 1918 coronation photograph records her emergence as queen, but the publication date should not be confused with the day of the ceremony.

Her cultural work matters alongside formal office. Te Papa’s curatorial account describes a prolific composer and poet whose songs contributed to Tongan expressive life. Objects associated with her also reveal how political relationships were made tangible. Fine mats and barkcloth could carry personal connections, commemorate public events and take part in mourning; they were more than accessories to royal portraits.

During the Second World War, the queen and people of Tonga raised funds for British Spitfire aircraft. A surviving barkcloth fragment records that effort, including the first payment in 1941. In 1952 the Tongan government purchased the Auckland residence Atalanga, which became her home during visits and later also accommodated Tongan students. These connections linked diplomacy with education and the practical needs of people moving between islands.

When Sālote died in 1965, a large ngatu accompanied the return of her body from New Zealand to Tonga. Reading such objects beside dated biographical records broadens the story beyond ceremonial appearances. It also leaves room for the work of often unnamed makers whose textiles helped sustain relationships within and beyond the royal household.
summary.zh:
萨洛特·图普三世的一生，把汤加王权同诗歌、表演及太平洋跨岛关系连接起来。她于1900年出生，1909年赴奥克兰上学，此后持续同新西兰往来。奥克兰报纸1918年刊登的加冕照片，记录她成为女王，但出版日期不应被当成仪式举行之日。

除正式职位外，她的文化工作同样重要。蒂帕帕博物馆研究将她描述为多产的作曲者与诗人，其歌曲参与构成汤加的表达生活。与她相关的物件也使政治关系获得可见形式。精细编席与树皮布可承载个人联系、纪念公共事件，并参与哀悼，不只是王室肖像中的配饰。

第二次世界大战期间，女王与汤加民众为英国“喷火”战斗机筹资。保存下来的树皮布残片纪念了这项努力，其中包括1941年的首次款项。1952年，汤加政府购入奥克兰的阿塔兰加住所，供她访问期间居住，后来也为汤加学生提供住宿。这些联系把外交同教育及岛际迁移者的实际需要相连。

1965年她去世后，一幅大型恩加图树皮布伴随遗体从新西兰返回汤加。将这些物件与有日期的生平材料并读，能使故事超出礼仪亮相，也让人注意那些姓名往往未被记录的制作者：他们的纺织品帮助维系王室内外的关系。

dateNote.en: 1900–1965 is the lifespan. The coronation milestone uses the documented year only; the 26 December newspaper date is not assigned to the ceremony. Tonga points are representative rather than inferred addresses.
dateNote.zh: 1900—1965年为生卒年。加冕节点仅用有据可查年份，不把12月26日报纸日期当作仪式日期。汤加点位为代表性位置，不推定具体住址。

title.en: Te reo Māori · Petition, language nests and public recognition
title.zh: 毛利语复兴 · 请愿、语言巢与公共承认

location.label: Wellington; petition and legislative context, not the whole movement

summary.en:
Māori language revitalization grew through collective action in homes, meeting places and public institutions. In 1972, Ngā Tamatoa, the Te Reo Māori Society and the New Zealand Māori Students’ Association gathered more than 30,000 signatures calling for Māori to be taught in schools. Hana Jackson and other organizers helped present the petition to Parliament on 14 September.

The work extended beyond requesting a school subject. Kōhanga reo brought fluent elders, preschool children and whānau together through immersion in language and values. The first opened at Pukeatua in Wainuiomata in 1982, and women supplied much of the organizing and daily labour. Families were participants in the educational institution rather than simply customers of it.

A claim heard by the Waitangi Tribunal in 1985 argued that te reo was a taonga protected under the Treaty. The Māori Language Act of 1987 established official status. These developments connected community transmission to public recognition, but legislation alone could not create fluent speakers or remove every barrier. The selected interval captures important institutional changes within a longer, continuing effort to sustain a living language across generations.
summary.zh:
毛利语复兴通过家庭、集会场所与公共机构中的集体行动发展。1972年，恩加塔马托阿、毛利语协会及新西兰毛利学生协会收集三万余份签名，要求学校教授毛利语。哈娜·杰克逊等组织者于9月14日协助向议会提交请愿。

行动并不止于增设一门课程。语言巢以全浸入语言与价值的方式，把流利使用母语的长者、学龄前儿童及家庭组织起来。第一个语言巢于1982年在怀努约马塔的普基阿图亚开办，女性承担了大量组织与日常劳动。家庭是教育机构的参与者，而不仅是服务购买者。

1985年怀唐伊审裁处听取诉求，主张毛利语属于《怀唐伊条约》保护的珍宝。1987年《毛利语言法》确立官方地位。这些发展把社区传承与公共承认相连，但法律本身不能自动造就流利使用者或消除全部障碍。本条所选区间记录长期持续的代际语言维护中的重要制度变化。

dateNote.en: 1972–1987 follows the petition through official recognition. Neither date marks the origin or end of te reo Māori or its revitalization.
dateNote.zh: 1972—1987年关注从请愿到官方承认的阶段。两端都不是毛利语或其复兴的绝对起讫。

title.en: Samoa’s 1918 influenza disaster · Disease and colonial responsibility
title.zh: 萨摩亚1918年流感灾难 · 疾病与殖民责任

location.label: Apia; port of entry and colonial administrative context

summary.en:
On 7 November 1918 the Talune reached Apia from Auckland with influenza aboard. Although the ship had faced quarantine in Fiji, authorities in New Zealand-administered Samoa allowed passengers to disembark without comparable restrictions. The disease spread into a society whose health services were unable to respond to the scale of the emergency.

Deaths affected households, leadership and the ordinary practices of mourning. Later estimates place the loss at about a fifth of the population, an indication of the catastrophe’s scale rather than a precise count of every death. Families faced illness, bereavement and disruption at the same time, while customary funerary observances became difficult to sustain.

Survivors blamed Administrator Robert Logan for the failure to quarantine the ship and for rejecting assistance from American Samoa. A subsequent commission found administrative neglect and poor judgment. The disaster therefore belongs to histories of government and colonial accountability as well as disease. Memories of the epidemic became part of the grievances that shaped relations with New Zealand. The 1919 endpoint marks the immediate official reckoning, not the end of grief or its political consequences.
summary.zh:
1918年11月7日，“塔卢内号”从奥克兰抵达阿皮亚，船上已有流感患者。虽然该船在斐济曾受到检疫，受新西兰管理的萨摩亚当局却允许乘客在没有类似限制的情况下上岸。疾病扩散时，当地卫生服务无法应对如此规模的紧急情况。

死亡冲击家庭、领导结构及平常的哀悼实践。后来估计，死亡约占人口五分之一，这用于说明灾难规模，而非每一死亡的精确清点。家庭同时面对疾病、丧亲与生活中断，传统丧葬仪式也难以维持。

幸存者责难行政长官罗伯特·洛根未实施船舶检疫，并拒绝美属萨摩亚提供援助。后续调查认定行政疏忽与判断失当。因此，这场灾难不仅属于疾病史，也属于政府治理与殖民责任史。疫情记忆成为影响对新西兰关系的怨愤之一。1919年的结束年份标示即时官方追责阶段，不代表悲痛或政治后果结束。

dateNote.en: 7 November 1918 is the ship’s arrival date in the inspected historical account; 1919 marks the immediate inquiry/administrative aftermath. Mortality is an approximate later estimate.
dateNote.zh: 已读历史资料把船舶到达日期定为1918年11月7日；1919年标示随后的调查与行政后果。死亡比例为后来的近似估计。

title.en: Banaba · Fertilizer, mining and forced displacement
title.zh: 巴纳巴 · 化肥、采矿与被迫迁离

location.label: Banaba; homeland and extraction site, not the relocation destination

summary.en:
Phosphate deposits identified on Banaba around 1900 connected a small Pacific island to agricultural production far away. Mining companies, followed by the British Phosphate Commission involving Britain, Australia and New Zealand, removed material used to fertilize farms. The value gained elsewhere depended on profound changes to the islanders’ land.

Extraction, wartime occupation and displacement combined during the twentieth century. Japanese forces occupied the island during the Second World War, and in 1945 Banaban people were relocated to Rabi in Fiji. The move separated many from a damaged homeland while allowing phosphate exploitation to continue. It should not be represented as an uncomplicated voluntary search for a new home.

Banaban writer Hele Christopher-Ikimotu connects this history to family memory and the difficulty of explaining a distinct identity within wider Pacific categories. Such testimony changes the scale of an account otherwise dominated by commodity flows and colonial institutions. The 1945 endpoint marks relocation in this selected history, not the disappearance of Banaban people or the termination of claims to land and identity. The map keeps Banaba visible rather than allowing the destination alone to replace the homeland.
summary.zh:
约1900年发现的磷矿，使太平洋小岛巴纳巴与远方农业生产相连。采矿公司及后来由英国、澳大利亚和新西兰参与的英国磷酸盐委员会，开采材料供农场施肥。别处获得的价值，以岛民土地的深刻改变为基础。

二十世纪的开采、战争占领与流离相互交织。第二次世界大战期间日军占领该岛，1945年巴纳巴人被迁到斐济拉比岛。迁移使许多人离开受损家园，同时让磷矿开采继续，不能写成简单自愿寻找新家的故事。

巴纳巴作者赫勒·克里斯托弗—伊基莫图，把这段历史与家庭记忆，以及在更宽泛太平洋分类中解释自身独特身份的困难相连。这样的证词，使通常由商品流通和殖民机构主导的叙述转向人的经验。1945年结束年份标示本条关注的迁离，不是巴纳巴人的消失，也不意味着土地与身份诉求终结。地图保留巴纳巴家园的位置，而非让迁入地取代家园。

dateNote.en: 1900–1945 links the discovery/mining era to relocation to Rabi. Extraction and Banaban community life continued afterward. Banaba and Rabi are distinct islands and are not collapsed into one point.
dateNote.zh: 1900—1945年连接矿产发现、采矿时代与迁往拉比。开采及巴纳巴社区生活此后继续。巴纳巴与拉比是不同岛屿，不合并为一点。

title.en: Day of Mourning, 1938 · Challenging a colonial anniversary
title.zh: 1938年哀悼日 · 质问殖民纪念

location.label: Australian Hall, Sydney; meeting venue

summary.en:
On 26 January 1938, while official celebrations marked 150 years since the First Fleet’s arrival, Aboriginal activists gathered in Sydney to declare a Day of Mourning. Their meeting at Australian Hall presented colonization through the loss of land, freedom and lives, challenging the triumphal story told by the public anniversary.

Organizers included Jack Patten, William Ferguson and William Cooper, with Pearl Gibbs among the participants in the wider campaign. The conference sought changes in education, treatment and citizenship. It was an Aboriginal-led political forum, supported by networks that had already been organizing in New South Wales and Victoria. Its existence makes clear that later rights movements did not begin from an absence of earlier political action.

The contrast with the official pageantry was especially stark. Aboriginal men brought from Menindee were compelled to take part in a staged colonial landing after Sydney Aboriginal people refused. The protest and reenactment offered sharply different accounts of whose history the anniversary represented. Subsequent annual observances carried the significance of mourning beyond the original meeting, while its specific demands belong to the political conditions of 1938.
summary.zh:
1938年1月26日，官方庆祝第一舰队抵达150周年之际，原住民行动者在悉尼集会，宣布这一天为哀悼日。澳大利亚厅的会议从土地、自由与生命的丧失讲述殖民，质问公共纪念中的胜利叙事。

组织者包括杰克·帕滕、威廉·弗格森与威廉·库珀，珀尔·吉布斯也参与相关运动。大会要求改变教育、待遇与公民资格。这是原住民主导的政治平台，由已在新南威尔士州和维多利亚州开展工作的网络支撑。它说明，后来的权利运动并非从没有政治行动的空白中开始。

官方庆典与之形成鲜明对照。悉尼原住民拒绝参与后，从梅宁迪带来的原住民男子被迫参加编排的殖民登陆重演。抗议与重演，对纪念日代表谁的历史给出截然不同的答案。后续年度纪念让哀悼意义超出原始会议，同时会议的具体诉求仍应放回1938年的政治条件中理解。

dateNote.en: 26 January 1938 is the meeting and protest date. Later commemorations are aftermath, not additional events assigned to that day.
dateNote.zh: 1938年1月26日为会议与抗议日期。后来的纪念属于影响，不归并为同日发生的事件。

sources.title: Day of Mourning
sources.evidenceNote: Inspected narrative: 26 January 1938 Australian Hall meeting, organizers, demands, refusal to join official reenactment and coercion of Menindee participants. No unqualified claim that Aboriginal political organizing began only in 1938 is adopted.

sources.title: Pearl Mary Gibbs
sources.evidenceNote: Inspected biography: 1901 birth, domestic service and support for Aboriginal girls, 1937 APA, 1938 Day of Mourning, 1941 broadcast, 1954–1957 Welfare Board service, 1956 fellowship, 1960 Dubbo hostel and 1983 death.

en: The protest coincided with the First Fleet anniversary.
Aboriginal organizers demanded equality and policy change.
Australian Hall provided a forum for an alternative history.
zh: 抗议与第一舰队纪念日同日。
原住民组织者要求平等与政策改变。
澳大利亚厅成为另一种历史叙述的平台。

reviewLimit.en: Museum and heritage biographies support the event and Gibbs’s participation. The synthesis does not turn the museum’s first-national-gathering description into a claim that earlier resistance or organizing did not exist.
reviewLimit.zh: 博物馆与文物机构传记支持事件及吉布斯参与。本条不把“首次全国性集会”扩写成此前不存在抵抗或组织行动。

title.en: Uluṟu–Kata Tjuṯa handback · Ownership and shared management
title.zh: 乌鲁鲁—卡塔丘塔归还 · 所有权与共同管理

location.label: Muṯitjulu community; representative handback ceremony setting

summary.en:
On 26 October 1985, title to Uluṟu–Kata Tjuṯa National Park was returned to Aṉangu, its Traditional Owners. The handback followed years of campaigning about land, tourism, mining and the protection of sacred places. It recognized relationships to Country that had continued even when park policy discouraged Aṉangu from remaining or moving there.

The ceremony took place at Muṯitjulu. Alongside the transfer, Aṉangu leased the park to the Australian National Parks and Wildlife Service for 99 years. A board with an Aṉangu majority was established in December. Ownership and management arrangements therefore changed together, while the park remained a place in which tourism, conservation and cultural responsibilities had to be negotiated.

This is a history of political work and institutional change, not the first moment when the landscape acquired cultural meaning. Nor should handback be treated as the end of every dispute about access, livelihoods or appropriate visitor behaviour. The event connects land-rights struggles elsewhere in Australia with the specific authority and responsibilities of the people who care for this Country. The point marks the community ceremony rather than a new territorial boundary.
summary.zh:
1985年10月26日，乌鲁鲁—卡塔丘塔国家公园的产权归还阿南古传统所有者。归还之前，人们已围绕土地、旅游、采矿及圣地保护进行多年争取。即使公园政策曾阻碍阿南古人在当地居留或流动，他们与祖地的关系仍持续存在。

仪式在穆蒂丘鲁社区举行。伴随产权转移，阿南古人将公园租给澳大利亚国家公园与野生动物管理机构99年。同年12月建立阿南古成员占多数的管理委员会。所有权与管理安排共同变化，旅游、保护及文化责任仍须在此协商。

这是一段政治努力与制度变化的历史，并非景观首次获得文化意义的时刻。归还也不意味着有关通行、生计或适当游客行为的争议全部结束。事件把澳大利亚其他地方的土地权利斗争，同守护这片祖地者的具体权威与责任联系起来。点位标示社区仪式，而非新的领土边界。

dateNote.en: 1985 covers the 26 October handback and December board establishment. It does not date the beginning of Aṉangu ownership in customary terms or the end of continuing governance.
dateNote.zh: 1985年涵盖10月26日归还与12月管理委员会建立。不表示阿南古传统所有关系的起点，也不表示后续治理结束。

sources.title: History of Uluṟu–Kata Tjuṯa National Park
sources.evidenceNote: Inspected land-rights section: continuing Aṉangu presence despite discouragement, campaigning, 26 October 1985 Muṯitjulu ceremony, 99-year lease and December majority-Aṉangu board. No territorial polygon or contemporary legal advice is inferred.

en: Title was returned to Aṉangu on 26 October 1985.
A 99-year lease accompanied handback.
The new management board had an Aṉangu majority.
zh: 产权于1985年10月26日归还阿南古人。
归还伴随99年租约。
新管理委员会由阿南古成员占多数。

reviewLimit.en: The park’s institutional history supports the dated arrangements. Aṉangu authority predates the legal transfer; the row does not equate title documents with the origin of customary responsibility.
reviewLimit.zh: 公园机构历史支持有日期的安排。阿南古权威早于法律转移；本条不把产权文件等同于传统责任的起源。

title.en: The Waitangi Tribunal · A forum for historical claims
title.zh: 怀唐伊审裁处 · 历史诉求的制度平台

location.label: Wellington; representative institutional and legislative center

summary.en:
The Treaty of Waitangi Act 1975 established a tribunal to investigate Māori claims about Crown breaches of Treaty principles. The institution emerged after a long history of petitions and protest, amid renewed activism over unresolved grievances. It created a formal place for evidence and argument concerning relationships that ordinary political processes had repeatedly failed to settle.

Its original reach was limited to contemporary Crown actions. In 1985, Parliament extended its jurisdiction back to 1840, opening a much larger field of historical inquiry. The change mattered because many claims concerned earlier land loss, state policies and the cumulative effects of dispossession. A date in an old document could now become part of a structured public investigation rather than being excluded simply as too remote.

The Tribunal hears evidence, determines whether claims are well founded and generally makes recommendations. This should not be confused with an automatic settlement or universal power to order every remedy. The ten-year interval marks institutional formation and expanded historical reach, not the beginning of Māori claims or their final resolution. Its history connects public institutions with continuing community efforts to make the past answerable to the present.
summary.zh:
1975年《怀唐伊条约法》设立审裁处，调查毛利人针对王权违反条约原则提出的诉求。该机构产生于长期请愿与抗争之后，当时人们正就未解决的不公重新展开行动。它为证据与论辩提供正式场所，处理普通政治程序反复未能解决的关系问题。

最初权限仅涉及当时的王权行为。1985年，议会把管辖范围追溯至1840年，打开更广泛的历史调查领域。这个变化很重要，因为许多诉求涉及早年的土地流失、国家政策及剥夺的累积影响。旧文献上的日期，可以进入有组织的公共调查，而不再仅因过于久远被排除。

审裁处听取证据，判断诉求是否成立，并通常提出建议。这不等于自动达成和解，也不意味着它对一切补救都有普遍命令权。十年区间标示机构形成及历史范围扩展，不是毛利诉求的开始或最终解决。其历史把公共机构同社区持续要求历史承担现实责任的努力相连。

dateNote.en: 1975–1985 tracks establishment and retrospective jurisdiction. The institution continued afterward; 1840 is the retrospective limit, not an additional start date for this record.
dateNote.zh: 1975—1985年关注设立与追溯管辖权扩展。机构此后继续运行；1840年是追溯界限，不是本条另一个起始年份。

sources.title: The Waitangi Tribunal: history, jurisdiction and role
sources.evidenceNote: Inspected institution’s own historical and explanatory sections: 1975 creation, original contemporary scope, 1985 extension to 1840, evidence hearings and recommendations. General recommendations are distinguished from limited statutory adjudicative powers.

en: The Tribunal was established in 1975.
Its historical jurisdiction expanded in 1985 to reach 1840.
Inquiry and recommendations do not automatically produce settlement.
zh: 审裁处于1975年设立。
1985年历史管辖权扩展至1840年。
调查与建议并不自动带来和解。

reviewLimit.en: The institution’s self-description supports historical scope and procedural distinctions. Individual reports and settlement legislation require separate inspection; this entry is not current legal advice.
reviewLimit.zh: 机构自身说明支持历史范围及程序区分。个别报告与和解立法须另行检阅；本条不提供当前法律意见。
